summary: Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she was supervised by Peter C. Bisschop and taught by Daniele Cuneo and Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied for a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).
Aritri Dutta is an external PhD student in Tibetology and religious studies at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Henk Blezer (attested 2026).

Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

Arlo Griffiths specializes in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Harvard and Leiden (PhD ~1999–2004 under Henk Bodewitz), he taught at Groningen (~2004–2005) and held professorships at Leiden (attested 2002–2008) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2008).

Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He served as professor of modern Arabic at INALCO from 1821, professor of Arabic at the Collège de France from 1833, and joined the Académie des Inscriptions in 1849.

Historian Arnold J. Toynbee studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Indologist and linguist Arthur Anthony Macdonell studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Leipzig (Doktor), and Oxford. He served as Deputy Professor (1888–1899) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888, succeeding Monier Monier-Williams in 1899.

Arthur Berriedale Keith worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Julius Eggeling at Edinburgh and Arthur Anthony Macdonell at Balliol College, Oxford. After serving in the Colonial Office (~1901–1914), he was professor at Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

Arthur Christensen was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1906) and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding Copenhagen's first chair of Oriental studies (1919–1945).

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at King's College London (~1857–1860) under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Heinrich August Jäschke, and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1880).
Arthur Evans was an archaeologist and historian. He was educated at Harrow School (~1866–1870) and Brasenose College (1870), and later taught John Marshall.
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Historian and Sinologist Arthur F. Wright studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard, working under John King Fairbank. He taught at Stanford University from 1947 (professor in 1958) before serving as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale (1959, 1961).

Indologist Arthur Llewellyn Basham studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held appointments at SOAS (Lecturer 1948, Reader and Professor 1953, 1957–1965) and served as Head of Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (~1965–1978).

Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer studied at Göttingen, Humboldt University of Berlin (under Fichte, Boeckh, and Wolf), and Jena, where he completed his doctorate in 1813. He held a lecturing post (Dozentur) at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1820.

Arthur Venis was an Indologist educated at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad and served as Professor of English (1881) and Principal (1885, 1888) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Arthur Waley was a Sinologist and Japanologist educated at King's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and later held an Honorary Lectureship in Chinese Poetry at SOAS (1948).

Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist educated at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig (PhD ~1901). He was an instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and subsequently professor of Sanskrit at the University of California, Berkeley (~1906–1938).
